title: Optimization of environmental DNA extraction and amplification methods for metabarcoding of deep-sea fish
author: Kawato, Yoshida, et al.
materials: To improve eDNA yield from each filter cartridge, we designed a modified eDNA extraction protocol using a commercial DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (QIAGEN, Valencia, CA, USA), which is based on the conventional protocol described by Miya et al. (2016), as described below (also see the graphical abstract). Any precautions against contamination during eDNA extraction were conducted according to the eDNA manual [30]. Differences among protocols are highlighted in Table 1.Table 1Differences in procedures of eDNA extraction between modified and conventional protocols.Table 1Step / Treatmentmodified protocolconventional protocolBefore lysis Filter cartridge treatment•Cut the outlet connection of the cartridge and divide into the filter unit and the housing•None Filter treatment•Detach the filter from the filter unit•Shred the filter to small fragments•NoneLysisSolution•440 µL PBS, 400 µL Buffer AL, 40 µL proteinase K, per filter•220 µL PBS, 200 µL Buffer AL, 20 µL proteinase K, per filter Lysis manner•Add the lysis solution into two microtubes•Incubate all filter fragments in two microtubes with occasional shaking•Add the lysis solution into the intact filter cartridge•Incubate the filter in the filter cartridge with rotary shaking Incubation•56 °C for 2 h•56 °C for 20 minElution from DNeasy column Elution buffer volume•200 µL per filter•100 µL per filter

steps.title: Thaw filter cartridge
steps.instruction: Transfer the Sterivex filter cartridge from the freezer to the bench and allow the RNAlater inside the cartridge to thaw at room temperature (15–25 °C).

steps.title: Remove RNAlater
steps.instruction: Aspirate RNAlater from the cartridge outlet as completely as possible using a vacuum pump equipped with a luer fitting.

steps.title: Place cartridge in petri dish
steps.instruction: Transfer the Sterivex cartridge onto a sterile petri dish.

steps.title: Open cartridge and isolate filter
steps.instruction: Cut the outlet connection with a TRUSCO tube cutter (TRUSCO Nakayama, Tokyo, Japan), separating the cartridge into the filter unit and the housing; place the filter unit on a second sterile petri dish.

steps.title: Halve filter and store
steps.instruction: Using a KAI sterile scalpel (Kai Corp., Tokyo, Japan), cut the filter along its edges and vertical lines to split it in half. Detach one half onto the second petri dish, keep the other half on the filter unit, and prevent drying.

steps.title: Fragment filter half
steps.instruction: On the petri dish, cut the transferred half into 32 equal‑sized fragments with the sterile scalpel and sterile sharp tweezers.

steps.title: Add fragments to lysis tube
steps.instruction: Collect all fragments with sterile tweezers and place them into a 2.0 mL microtube containing 220 µL PBS (‑), 200 µL Buffer AL* and 20 µL proteinase K* (both from the QIAGEN DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit).

steps.title: Mix lysate thoroughly
steps.instruction: Tightly close the tube lid and mix the lysate by hand‑shaking.

steps.title: Fragment second filter half
steps.instruction: Transfer the remaining half from the filter unit to a petri dish and cut it into 32 fragments as described in the previous fragmentation step.

steps.title: Lysis of second fragment set
steps.instruction: Repeat the addition of fragments to a new 2.0 mL microtube with the same lysis solution (220 µL PBS, 200 µL Buffer AL, 20 µL proteinase K) and hand‑shake to mix.

steps.title: Incubate lysates
steps.instruction: Place both microtubes in an incubator set to 56 °C and incubate for 2 h, shaking occasionally.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysates
steps.instruction: After incubation, centrifuge the microtubes at 15,000 × g for 1 min.

steps.title: Collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from each tube into a new 2.0 mL microtube, yielding approximately 880 µL total volume.

steps.title: Add ethanol to lysate
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL of 96–100 % ethanol to the combined supernatant and mix thoroughly by pipetting.

steps.title: Load sample onto spin column
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 700 µL of the ethanol‑mixed solution into a DNeasy mini spin column (QIAGEN) placed in a collection tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge column (first load)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 6000 × g for 1 min and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Load remaining sample
steps.instruction: Repeat the loading (up to 700 µL) and centrifugation steps until all of the lysate has passed through the column.

steps.title: Replace collection tube
steps.instruction: Discard the used collection tube and place the column into a new collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with AW1
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer AW1* to the column, centrifuge at 6000 × g for 1 min, and discard the flow‑through.

steps.title: Replace collection tube again
steps.instruction: Discard the collection tube and place the column into another fresh collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with AW2 (first)
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Buffer AW2* to the column and centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min.

steps.title: Dry column
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, place the column back in an empty collection tube, and centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 1 min to remove residual buffer.

steps.title: Move column to elution tube
steps.instruction: Discard the collection tube and transfer the column into a new 1.5 mL or 2.0 mL microtube.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Buffer AE* directly onto the membrane, incubate at room temperature (15–25 °C) for 1 min, then centrifuge at 6000 × g for 1 min to collect the eluate.

steps.title: Optional second elution
steps.instruction: If desired, repeat the elution step with a fresh tube to increase DNA recovery.

steps.title: Store eluted DNA
steps.instruction: Discard the column, cap the tube, label appropriately, and store the eluted eDNA solution in a freezer until use.

steps.title: Purify first PCR product
steps.instruction: Clean the first‑PCR amplicons using AMPure XP beads (Beckman Courter, Brea, CA, USA) according to the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Prepare second PCR mix
steps.instruction: Set up a 10 µL second‑PCR reaction containing 1× Ex Taq buffer (Takara Bio, Shiga, Japan), 0.2 mM each dNTP, 0.5 µM forward primer, 0.5 µM reverse primer, 0.5 U Ex Taq polymerase (Takara Bio), and 2.0 µL of the purified first‑PCR product.

steps.title: Run second PCR thermal cycle
steps.instruction: Thermal cycle: 94 °C for 2 min; then 12 cycles of 94 °C for 30 s, 60 °C for 30 s, 72 °C for 30 s; final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Purify second PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the second‑PCR amplicons with AMPure XP beads (Beckman Courter) following the standard protocol.

steps.title: Construct library and sequence
steps.instruction: Complete the paired‑end library preparation and submit the library for Illumina MiSeq sequencing (Illumina, San Diego, CA, USA) using 2 × 300 bp read configuration.
